title: Heat transfer equation

items.label: q
items.meaning: heat absorbed (+) or released (−) by the substance; energy units such as J

items.label: m
items.meaning: mass of the substance whose temperature changes (g)

items.label: c
items.meaning: specific heat capacity of that substance (J/(g·°C) or J/(g·K))

items.label: \Delta T
items.meaning: change in temperature of the substance, final minus initial (°C or K; the size of the change is the same on both scales)

caution: Use the total mass of the material that actually changes temperature (e.g., the whole solution, not just the solute). The equation uses specific heat capacity with mass; with molar heat capacity, use moles instead of mass (6.4.A.5). Report q with the correct significant figures.

title: Heat from moles and molar enthalpy

items.label: q
items.meaning: heat absorbed (+) or released (−) by the system (kJ)

items.label: n
items.meaning: amount of the substance undergoing the phase transition or reaction (mol)

items.label: \Delta H_{\text{molar}}
items.meaning: molar enthalpy of the phase transition (fusion, vaporization) or of the reaction (kJ/mol)

caution: The CED states this as a relationship (amount in moles times molar enthalpy), not as a written equation. Sign matters: a positive ΔH means heat is absorbed (endothermic) and a negative ΔH means heat is released (exothermic). The reverse phase change has the opposite sign (ΔH_condensation = −ΔH_vaporization). For a reaction, n must match the substance the molar enthalpy is quoted per mole of. Temperature stays constant during a phase change of a pure substance, so q = mcΔT does not apply there.
ced_evidence: 6.5.A / 6.6.A "amount of the substance in moles and the molar enthalpy"

title: Enthalpy of reaction from average bond energies

items.label: \Delta H_{\text{reaction}}
items.meaning: estimated enthalpy change of the reaction (kJ per mole of reaction as written)

items.label: \Sigma E_{\text{bonds broken}}
items.meaning: sum of average bond energies of all bonds in the reactant molecules (kJ/mol); energy required

items.label: \Sigma E_{\text{bonds formed}}
items.meaning: sum of average bond energies of all bonds in the product molecules (kJ/mol); energy released

caution: Count every bond in every molecule, using the balanced equation's coefficients. Because average bond energies are used, the result is an estimate. If energy released exceeds energy required, ΔH is negative (exothermic); if energy required exceeds energy released, ΔH is positive (endothermic).
ced_evidence: 6.7.A.2 "adding up the average bond energies of all the bonds in the reactant molecules"

title: Standard enthalpy of reaction from enthalpies of formation

items.label: \Delta H^{\circ}_{\text{reaction}}
items.meaning: standard enthalpy change of the reaction (kJ per mole of reaction as written)

items.label: \Sigma
items.meaning: sum over all species on that side of the balanced equation

items.label: \Delta H_f^{\circ}{}_{\text{products}}
items.meaning: standard enthalpies of formation of the products (kJ/mol), from a table

items.label: \Delta H_f^{\circ}{}_{\text{reactants}}
items.meaning: standard enthalpies of formation of the reactants (kJ/mol), from a table

caution: Products minus reactants, not the reverse. Multiply each tabulated value by its coefficient in the balanced equation before summing. Values are standard enthalpies from tables.
